method: 30 comments drawn with random.seed(20261019) from the 71 distinct v22 inline comments that six of six reviewers reported and Martian's gpt-5.2 judge matched to no golden comment; each checked against the code at the fork's PR head by one of three independent model agents instructed to refute, with cited lines; fetched 2026-10-19

sample.comment: [P2] **Keep the original public result key.** With `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`, `BaseQueryBuilder.process_results` renames `count` to this replacement string, but the endpoint still serializes the original `count()` key and silently substitutes zero (`api/serializers/snuba.py:92`). Trigger: any eligible nonempty count chart with that flag; an isolated execution of the actual transformation, result-processing and serialization functions reproduced 10 becoming 0—preserve/remap the original field identity and add flag-enabled tests.
sample.evidence: error_upsampling.py:95 rewrites count() to 'upsampled_count() as count'; builder/base.py:746 stores function_alias_map['count'].field = that string and process_results (base.py:1566-1618) renames the row key to it when transform_alias_to_input_format is set, while bases/organization_events.py:605-608 serializes with resolve_axis_column('count()', ..., True) = 'count()' and serializers/snuba.py uses r.get(column, 0). organization_events_stats.py:205 sets the flag from transformAliasToInputFormat=1 and passes it to timeseries_query (snuba/discover.py:330).

sample.comment: [P2] This credential-ID-only lookup misses delegated Google connections: `connectedCalendarsHandler` passes the in-memory ID `-1`, while cache writes use positive persisted credential IDs (`delegationCredential/server.ts:619–646`). Trigger: a delegation user with populated cache opens calendar settings; status is null and both cache actions disappear. Resolve the authenticated user's persisted cache identity for both status and deletion, as the delegated read path above already does.
sample.evidence: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29 passes connectedCalendars credentialIds (CalendarManager.ts:64 = credential.id; in-memory delegation credentials are built with id -1 at delegationCredential/server.ts:86) into getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, whose groupBy at calendar-cache.repository.ts:177 matches only persisted ids; cache writes for delegated users go through getCredentialForCalendarCache (server.ts:623-646) with the positive DB credential id, and getCachedAvailability (repository.ts:95-119) already reads delegated cache by userId. CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:68-71 then hides the whole dropdown (canDisconnect false for delegation, hasCache null).

sample.comment: [P2] Formatting the entire accumulated prefix on every iteration makes large SQLite batches quadratic in allocation and copy work, before SQL execution or another cancellation check. The new 32,767-ID tag batches exercise this path; an isolated check of this exact loop allocated about 1.26 GB cumulatively for just 16,000 IDs and a 101 KB final string. Use a linear builder/`strconv.AppendInt`, as the numeric-list construction at lines 387–395 already does.
sample.evidence: xorm_store.go:608-612 (new in this PR) builds the SQLite IN-list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` per ID, reformatting the whole prefix each iteration; the path is taken when GetDBType()==SQLite and AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize>999, and cleanup_test.go adds a 32767-ID case. Lines 387-395 already use strconv.AppendInt. Perf-only, so robustness rather than a functional defect.

sample.comment: [nit] This warning makes a requirement of the CLI compatibility commands sound mandatory for the Operator, unnecessarily directing users to enable a preview feature. With `rolling-updates` absent and either documented update strategy selected, `UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35–42` still dispatches to implementations that never check this flag (`AlwaysRecreateUpgradeLogic.java:40–42`, `RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic.java:49–58`); remove or narrow the Operator-failure claim.
sample.evidence: advanced-configuration.adoc:446-450 (added by the PR) says the Operator will fail without rolling-updates, but UpgradeLogicFactory.java dispatches only to RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic / AlwaysRecreateUpgradeLogic, neither of which checks any feature, and a grep of all 67 operator/src/main/java files finds no reference to ROLLING_UPDATES or update-compatibility; only the CLI commands (UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata.java) gate on the feature. Likely forward-looking text, so a maintainer may keep it.

sample.comment: [P1] This unconditionally dereferences `organization_context.member`, although that field explicitly permits `None` (`organization/model.py:344–346`) and organization API-key authentication legitimately has no user membership (`authentication.py:272`, `permissions.py:170–180`). Consequently, previously valid audit-log requests now raise `AttributeError` even without opting in. Trigger: an authorized organization API key requests audit logs. Fix: guard absent membership and evaluate advanced eligibility only when requested, preserving the normal paginator fallback.
sample.evidence: organization_auditlogs.py:71 dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally (outside the use_optimized check at :73); model.py:344-346 declares member Optional and None for non-members; ApiKeyAuthentication returns transform_auth(None, key) at authentication.py:272 and OrganizationPermission builds access via from_rpc_auth for request.auth without a user (permissions.py:170-180), so an org:write API key passes OrganizationAuditPermission (organization.py:110-111) and hits AttributeError.

sample.comment: [P2] **Make repeated member additions idempotent.** `Group#add` unconditionally inserts a join row (`app/models/group.rb:272–274`), so selecting an existing member—or pressing Add again with the retained selection—violates the unique membership index and prevents later names from being added. Deduplicate/skip existing memberships with concurrency-safe handling, and clear successfully submitted selections.
sample.evidence: group.rb:272-274 `add` is `self.users.push(user)` on a has_many :through, which inserts a group_users row immediately; group_user.rb schema shows UNIQUE index on (group_id,user_id), so re-adding raises RecordNotUnique inside the usernames loop at groups_controller.rb:71-75 and aborts later names. admin-group.js.es6:61-65 has `// TODO: should clear the input`, confirming the selection is retained.

sample.comment: [nit] **Do not override PasswordField's visibility-dependent type.** The newly selected component computes its input type and then spreads `props` (`Input.tsx:36–39`), so this retained `type="password"` wins even after visibility is toggled. Trigger: click the setup password's eye button; its icon/text change to Hide password, but the input remains masked. Fix: remove the explicit type from this caller.
sample.evidence: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:36-39 sets type={isPasswordVisible ? 'text' : 'password'} and then spreads {...props}; EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:176 passes type="password" to PasswordField, so the toggle changes the icon/label but the input stays masked.

sample.comment: [P2] **Rewrite count semantics inside supported expressions too.** Exact whole-string matching leaves `equation|count() / 100` and `count() as total` unchanged, so equivalent count metrics refer to different populations; mixed axes can also reintroduce the raw `count` alias. Trigger: one weight-10 error yields bare count 10 but count/100 of 0.01; isolated helper execution confirmed the equation is untouched—transform parsed aggregate nodes while preserving aliases, with equation-only and mixed-axis tests.
sample.evidence: Exact whole-string matching is pre-existing upstream design, not something this PR introduced: the PR base (a5d2909) error_upsampling.py:114-125 and current getsentry/sentry main both match `column_lower in function_conversions`, so equations like `equation|count() / 100` are left untouched upstream too. The PR's real change at head :92-95 is dropping the eps/epm/sample_* conversions and include_alias, which the comment does not mention.

sample.comment: [P2] These UTC clock minutes are target-date values, but `getWorkingHours` uses today's timezone offset (`availability.ts:72–85`), while slot generation already corrects future DST (`lib/slots.ts:102–110`). Trigger: querying summer New York 09:00–17:00 hours during winter yields a valid 13:00Z opening slot that this check rejects against the stored 14:00Z start. Normalize weekly boundaries to the requested date before comparing.
sample.evidence: slots.ts:139-146 compares the slot's UTC minutes to workingHour.startTime/endTime, which come from getUserAvailability.ts:210 `getWorkingHours({ timeZone }, availability)`; availability.ts:72-74 derives utcOffset from `dayjs().tz(timeZone)` (today's offset). lib/slots.ts:102-110 shifts generated slots by organizerDSTDiff for the target date, so a winter query for a summer date yields 13:00Z slots that are rejected against the 14:00Z stored start.

sample.comment: [P1] **Require verified primary authentication before accepting a backup code.** The password/provider gates at lines 113–128 trust the presence of `totpCode`, but this new branch takes precedence without validating that value, allowing recovery codes to replace both factors. Trigger: a valid unused backup code accompanied by an arbitrary nonempty TOTP field and an incorrect password. Fix: require a verified password or server-validated external-login continuation independently of the selected second factor.
sample.evidence: next-auth-options.ts:113-129 skip the provider and password checks whenever credentials.totpCode is non-empty, and the new branch at 131-156 runs when backupCode is present without ever validating totpCode, so a valid backup code plus any non-empty totpCode and a wrong password authenticates. The totpCode-skips-password pattern is pre-existing, but the PR extends it to recovery codes with no second check.

sample.comment: [P2] **Do not persist rates production rejects.** Truthiness plus `float()` accepts negative, greater-than-one, nonfinite and string rates, whereas production requires numeric values in `(0,1]` (`event_manager.py:785–787`) and does not remove this pre-inserted key on rejection. Trigger: an allowlisted fixture with rate 1.5 persists that rate and can acquire `times_seen=int(1/1.5)=0`; isolated helper execution confirmed invalid rates survive—reuse production derivation/validation rather than weakening it in the shared factory.
sample.evidence: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling at factories.py:344-357 is byte-identical to the PR base (a5d2909 factories.py:345-358) and is pre-existing upstream test-fixture code; the mechanism (truthiness + float(), production range check at event_manager.py:785-787, times_seen=int(1/rate) at :1560-1565) is accurate but only bites a test that deliberately passes an invalid rate, which is fixture convenience rather than a PR defect.

sample.comment: [nit] Unlike startup validation at lines 81–85, late registration assumes a newly deployed grant has a unique shortcut and blindly overwrites its existing owner. Trigger: a distinct dynamically deployed grant reuses a shortcut, then issues its first token; previously issued tokens now decode as the new grant, including unknown-context tokens if it reuses `na`. Use one atomic, collision-checking registration path for startup and both lazy updates.
sample.evidence: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:110-114 and 125-133 do unconditional `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` with no collision check, whereas postInit lines 81-85 validates via map sizes; `na` is seeded at line 78 and can be overwritten the same way. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:91 decodes via getGrantTypeByShortcut, so earlier tokens would resolve to the new grant. Requires a dynamically deployed grant with a colliding shortcut, hence an edge case.

sample.comment: [P2] The denial key drops `IdentityType`, so different principals share negative decisions. Both anonymous and renderer identities use ID `0` (`pkg/services/authn/clients/render.go:43–50`): an anonymous denial followed by a renderer check of the same dashboard/folder returns false before the renderer's wildcard grant at lines 446–447. sample.comment: [P2] A thumbnail-only preference now controls destructive rewriting of the original: when false, `downsize_instructions` reads only frame zero (`optimized_image.rb:129`), permanently deleting animation before upload creation. It also overrides the distinct avatar policy applied later at `upload.rb:83-98`. Trigger: an oversized animated original with animated thumbnails disabled, including an avatar with animated avatars enabled. Preserve original frames during downsizing and apply thumbnail/avatar preferences only to their intended outputs.
sample.evidence: uploads_controller.rb:66-67 rewrites the original tempfile in place via OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails); optimize at optimized_image.rb:155 only picks the gifsicle path when allow_animation is truthy, otherwise downsize_instructions (:126-135) uses `#{from}[0]` (frame zero only), so an oversized animated GIF is de-animated before Upload.create_for, which later applies allow_animated_avatars at upload.rb:83-98 to an already-flattened file.

sample.comment: [nit] This test assumes the reader is scheduled before deletion finishes, but no synchronization establishes that: if its first timeslice occurs after line 155, the loop executes zero GETs and the test passes without exercising concurrent reads. Coordinate reader startup and deletion with a latch/barrier and assert actual read activity; preferably make the deletion/lookup overlap deterministic.
sample.evidence: GroupTest.java:139-149 starts the reader thread with no latch; lines 152-155 delete 100 groups then set deletedAll, and line 157 only asserts no exceptions, never that any GET ran. The zero-GET scenario is literally possible but practically negligible given 100 sequential HTTP deletes, so this is a low-value nit, not a wrong claim.

sample.comment: [P2] `device_limit` is absent from `conf/defaults.ini`, while environment and CLI overrides enumerate only existing INI keys before this parsing runs (`setting.go:686–700,782–811,916–923`). Register `device_limit = 0` in shipped defaults and test environment/CLI-only loading.
sample.evidence: setting.go:686-698 and 782-811 iterate only keys already present in the parsed INI, and conf/defaults.ini has no device_limit under [auth.anonymous] (grep at head, nor in sample.ini); setting.go:1654 then reads MustInt64(0) and anonstore/database.go:109 treats 0 as no limit, so GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is silently dropped.

Removing a member whose `primary_group_id` equals this group now leaves that affiliation on their posts (`app/serializers/post_serializer.rb:96–102`); clear the matching primary-group reference atomically with membership removal.

Trigger: open More on an editable Grafana alert in list v2, including a paused alert; pass UID/paused state to `MenuItemPauseRule` (or load Ruler on demand), and test the interaction rather than the new four-item menu count.

sample.comment: [P1] A matching date override returns before `busy.every`, so overrides now bypass calendar bookings, buffers, and booking-limit blocks rather than just replacing weekly hours. Trigger: a 10:00–12:00 UTC override with an existing 10:00–11:00 busy interval still advertises 10:00 (reproduced); continue through the busy checks after validating the override.

sample.comment: [P2] Searching for any working-hours interval that excludes the slot treats alternative shifts as an intersection and removes ordinary availability even without overrides. Trigger: Monday 09:00–12:00 plus 14:00–17:00 rejects every morning slot against the afternoon range and vice versa (reproduced); accept full containment in at least one applicable interval instead.

sample.comment: [P2] **Preserve federated-group immutability** Delegating the legacy CombinedRule hook here now discards `rule.group.source_tenants`, so this hardcoded false removes the existing federation immutability check. Trigger: an external-rule editor views a federated Mimir group in the legacy table; Edit is enabled even though sibling `RulesGroup` still disallows federated editing. Preserve/pass the group-level federation flag through the adapter.

sample.comment: [nit] `factory.shutdown()` closes workers but never sets the strategy’s shutdown event, leaving its daemon commit loop and retained callbacks alive after every successful test. The seven new uptime factory tests use the same cleanup pattern. Register cleanup immediately and close/join the returned strategy as well as the factory, including assertion-failure paths.
sample.evidence: test_queue_consumer.py:415-421 only calls factory.shutdown(); result_consumer.py:180-185 shuts down queue_pool but never touches the strategy, whose daemon commit_thread (queue_consumer.py:268-291) loops on shutdown_event, set only by close()/terminate() (335-342). The seven uptime tests (test_results_consumer.py:1731-2004) likewise call factory.shutdown() with no consumer.close()/join().

sample.comment: [P2] `TagDevice` returns nil before consulting storage when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is absent (`impl.go:119–122`), but this authentication gate interprets that no-op as admission. Trigger: an anonymous API request without that optional header arrives at full capacity; ordinary frontend requests can also omit it before asynchronous fingerprint initialization finishes (`public/app/core/services/backend_srv.ts:95–102,159–162`). Establish and enforce device admission independently of optional telemetry headers, with explicit bootstrap handling.
sample.evidence: Mechanism is as described (impl.go:119-122 returns nil with no X-Grafana-Device-Id; client.go:44-50 only denies on ErrDeviceLimitReached), but this is the deliberate upstream design: current grafana/grafana main has the identical TagDevice short-circuit (impl.go:137-141) and the identical Authenticate gate, so the device limit is defined over tagged devices and header-less requests are intentionally untracked rather than a defect of this PR.

sample.comment: [P2] Retry cleanup also deletes successfully scheduled rows, destroying their cancellation reference while the SMS remains queued at Twilio. Trigger: overlapping runs both read count 1; one saves `scheduled: true/referenceId`, the other records count 2, and the next cleanup deletes the future reminder—booking cancellation subsequently cannot find it (`handleCancelBooking.ts:454–458`). Restrict exhausted cleanup and failure updates to unscheduled rows and coordinate scheduling attempts. Reproduced with mocked services.
sample.evidence: scheduleSMSReminders.ts:29-45 deleteMany has an OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no scheduled/method filter, and the failure updates at lines 179-186 and 190-197 write retryCount from the stale in-memory value regardless of scheduled state; a successful row (scheduled: true, referenceId set at 169-177) whose retryCount reached 2 via an overlapping run is deleted next tick, so handleCancelBooking.ts:454-458 never sees it. Needs overlapping cron runs, so edge-case.

sample.comment: [P2] All mock occurrences share this ID, and `IssueOccurrence.__eq__` compares only IDs (`issues/issue_occurrence.py:181–184`), so the new result and producer-call assertions accept wrong fingerprints and priorities. The existing test already expects `val1` at line 537 while evaluating `group_key` at line 548; an isolated check confirmed these unequal fingerprints compare equal—compare serialized fields or explicitly assert hook arguments and correct that expected key.
sample.evidence: issue_occurrence.py:181-184 defines __eq__ as id equality; test_detector.py:251-252 gives every mock occurrence the fixed id eb4b0acf..., so fingerprint/priority mismatches are invisible. test_detector.py:536-548 builds the expected occurrence for 'val1' but evaluates group key 'group_key', and test_state_results_multi_group builds occurrence_2 with value 6 for a group whose value is 10; both pass only because of id-only equality.

sample.comment: [P1] Every replacement strategy receives the same factory-owned pool, but the previous strategy permanently shuts it down in `close()` (`queue_consumer.py:338`). On the first normal partition rebalance, subsequent `put()` calls raise `ShutDown`, and the catch at `queue_consumer.py:317–325` acknowledges results that never ran. Allocate a fresh pool/tracker per assignment or preserve reusable workers with assignment-isolated state; a focused Python 3.13 reproduction confirmed zero processed results with an acknowledged offset.
sample.evidence: result_consumer.py:133-137 builds one FixedQueuePool per factory and create_thread_queue_parallel_worker (:244-259) hands that same self.queue_pool to every strategy; SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/join (queue_consumer.py:335-345) call queue_pool.shutdown(), which sets worker.shutdown and q.shutdown() at :231-243. Arroyo's processor closes/joins the strategy on revoke (processor.py:288-296) and calls create_with_partitions on reassignment (:194), after which put() at :212 raises queue.ShutDown, caught by the broad except at :317-325 that marks the offset complete for the commit loop.

sample.comment: [P2] `appStoreMetadata` preserves directory-name keys, not public slugs (`apps.metadata.generated.ts:98,104,109–110,146`), so valid installed Google, Outlook, Lark, Teams and Zoom apps return 404 here. Trigger: an authenticated request using the real `google-calendar` slug. Fix: resolve metadata by `.slug`, or select and index by `App.dirName`.
sample.evidence: appStoreMetaData.ts:11-14 copies rawAppStoreMetadata keys unchanged, and apps.metadata.generated.ts:98,104,109-110,146 keys are directory names (googlecalendar, larkcalendar, office365calendar, office365video, zoomvideo); googlecalendar/_metadata.ts has slug "google-calendar" and seed-app-store.ts:245 creates App.slug "google-calendar", so app-credential.ts:50 `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` is undefined and line 53 returns 404.

sample.comment: [P2] **Allow identifier-based deletion without a Ruler DTO** `canDelete && rulerRule` at line 165 suppresses Delete for every new Prometheus-only Grafana row, despite the folder delete grant. sample.comment: [P2] **Refresh enabled state on every completion path.** Successful enablement now defers `onEnable()` until the dedicated Close button, while Escape/outside dismissal invokes only `onOpenChange`; the parent invalidates `viewer.me` exclusively in `onEnable` (`pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64–67`). sample.evidence: EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:134-136 now only does setStep(DisplayBackupCodes) on 200 (diff shows the removed `onEnable()`), and onEnable is invoked solely by the Close button at lines 263-270; Dialog onOpenChange at line 166 maps to two-factor-auth.tsx:64 which only toggles the open flag, while viewer.me invalidation lives in onEnable at lines 65-68.
